structures.name: Proximal posterior spinal veins
structures.description: Descends on the posterior cervical cord surface from posterior medullary connections.
structures.notes: These are components/arrangements of the dorsal spinal network, not universally interchangeable single-vessel names.

referenceFields.Course: Descends on the posterior cervical cord surface from posterior medullary connections.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Posterior cord and connected medullary/fissural channels.
referenceFields.Outflow: Cervical perimedullary network and radicular/foraminal connections.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Dorsal cervical cord, posterior medulla and foramen magnum.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Inside the canal, anterior to the posterior atlas arch; not in the bony vertebral venous plexus itself.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Dorsal cord surface; foramen magnum; C1 posterior arch Modelling interpretation Limit the initial model to the craniovertebral segment. Add local radicular outflow without drawing an entire spinal system.
referenceFields.Variants: Median and posterolateral forms and variable connections.
referenceFields.Naming: These are components/arrangements of the dorsal spinal network, not universally interchangeable single-vessel names.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I10, I19. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S08. Bradac p. 144; Neuroangio posterior spinal MRI.
referenceFields.Alternate names: Posterior median spinal vein; Posterolateral spinal veins

structures.name: Median posterior medullary vein
structures.description: Forms from paired posterior/restiform-body channels and continues caudally as posterior spinal drainage.
structures.notes: Posterior/dorsal label depends on source.

referenceFields.Course: Forms from paired posterior/restiform-body channels and continues caudally as posterior spinal drainage.
referenceFields.Outflow: Posterior spinal and connected lateral medullary network.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Posterior medulla and obex region.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Posterior to medulla inside the foramen magnum/cervical canal; clear of occipital bone and posterior atlas arch.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Obex; posterior medulla; posterior cord surface Modelling interpretation Add the caudal dorsal midline route and paired upper convergence. Avoid copying the ventral anterior spinal course.
referenceFields.Variants: Continuity and size vary.
referenceFields.Naming: Posterior/dorsal label depends on source.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I19, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Alternate names: Posteromedian medullary vein; Median dorsal medullary vein

structures.name: Tentorial sinuses, right
structures.description: Courses within the tentorium between a bridging-vein entry and a transverse, straight or petrosal sinus endpoint.
structures.notes: Sinus family, not an extra cerebellar pial vein or a universal persistence of one embryonic channel. Flattened representative intradural channel; its body is fitted to the registered tentorial leaf.

referenceFields.Course: Courses within the tentorium between a bridging-vein entry and a transverse, straight or petrosal sinus endpoint.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Cerebellar surface veins; some basal/cerebral venous variants.
referenceFields.Outflow: Transverse, straight or petrosal dural drainage.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Tentorial leaf above cerebellum and below supratentorial brain.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Free tentorial dura defines most of the channel. Bony attachment applies at petrous/transverse margins, not throughout the leaf.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Tentorial plane; bridging entry; tentorial attachment; receiving sinus Modelling interpretation Add a flattened intradural route constrained by a tentorial surface. Do not snap it to the occipital or petrous bone along its whole length.
referenceFields.Variants: Highly variable position and tributaries.
referenceFields.Naming: Sinus family, not an extra cerebellar pial vein or a universal persistence of one embryonic channel.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I11, I22. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S04, S11. Bradac pp. 132, 138 and 148; Neuroangio tentorial images.

structures.name: Superior cerebellar hemispheric veins, right
structures.description: Courses over superior hemispheric folia towards Galenic/vermians, petrosal collectors or a tentorial/transverse endpoint.
structures.notes: Family record; named trunks vary.

referenceFields.Course: Courses over superior hemispheric folia towards Galenic/vermians, petrosal collectors or a tentorial/transverse endpoint.
referenceFields.Outflow: Galenic, petrosal or tentorial/transverse groups, depending on location.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Superior cerebellar hemisphere beneath the tentorium.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: The pial segment follows cerebellum. A bridging terminal segment reaches tentorial dura or a sinus; only that endpoint is dural.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Superior cerebellar surface; tentorium; selected sinus endpoint Modelling interpretation Add a medial and a lateral representative with different outflow options. Avoid forcing every superior vein through the superior vermian trunk.
referenceFields.Variants: Relative dominance varies markedly.
referenceFields.Naming: Family record; named trunks vary.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I07, I11, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S04. Bradac pp. 145-148; Neuroangio cerebellar surfaces.

structures.name: Vein of the great horizontal fissure, right
structures.description: Follows the horizontal fissural region on the anterior/lateral cerebellum towards the petrosal network.
structures.notes: Anterior cerebellar vein can be used more broadly; bind the alias to the documented course.

referenceFields.Course: Follows the horizontal fissural region on the anterior/lateral cerebellum towards the petrosal network.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Superior and inferior anterior cerebellar tributaries.
referenceFields.Outflow: Petrosal vein and related fissural collectors.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Great horizontal fissure and anterior cerebellar hemisphere.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Horizontal fissure; anterior cerebellar surface; petrosal junction Modelling interpretation Reconcile the course with the existing cerebellopontine fissure vein before creating an overlapping trunk.
referenceFields.Variants: Size and connections vary.
referenceFields.Naming: Anterior cerebellar vein can be used more broadly; bind the alias to the documented course.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I21, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels

structures.name: Anterior cerebellar hemispheric veins, right
structures.description: Converges across the anterior cerebellar surface towards fissural and petrosal collectors.
structures.notes: Do not confuse these surface tributaries with the short petrosal bridging trunk.

referenceFields.Course: Converges across the anterior cerebellar surface towards fissural and petrosal collectors.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Petrosal cerebellar surface beside the middle cerebellar peduncle.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Faces the posterior petrous surface, but lies on cerebellum rather than plastered against bone.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Anterior cerebellar surface; middle cerebellar peduncle; petrosal collector Modelling interpretation Use superior and inferior surface representatives feeding the existing fissure/petrosal trunks.
referenceFields.Variants: Can dominate cerebellar outflow.
referenceFields.Naming: Do not confuse these surface tributaries with the short petrosal bridging trunk.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I07, I08. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S04. Bradac p. 148; Neuroangio anterior surface dominance.

structures.name: Inferior cerebellar hemispheric veins, right
structures.description: Runs over the inferior/posterior cerebellar surface to direct transverse/sigmoid or short tentorial drainage.
structures.notes: Extension of current anatomy, not a wholly missing family.

referenceFields.Course: Runs over the inferior/posterior cerebellar surface to direct transverse/sigmoid or short tentorial drainage.
referenceFields.Outflow: Transverse or sigmoid sinus, with variable tentorial and vermian connections.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Posteroinferior cerebellar surface.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Remote from the occipital inner table until the terminal bridging segment reaches the transverse/sigmoid dural region.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Inferior cerebellar surface; transverse groove; sigmoid groove Modelling interpretation Keep the existing veins but add representative direct dural outflow; revise the current sole inferior-vermian connection.
referenceFields.Variants: Can substitute for a small inferior vermian group.
referenceFields.Naming: Extension of current anatomy, not a wholly missing family.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I07. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S04. Bradac p. 148; Neuroangio inferior surface examples. Existing IDs: vein.inferior_hemispheric.left, vein.inferior_hemispheric.right

structures.name: Vein of the lateral recess of the fourth ventricle, right
structures.description: From the cerebellomedullary/lateral recess region, emerges by the lateral aperture and curves around the floccular region into the ascending CPA component.
structures.notes: Sources partition the intraventricular, fissural and ascending components differently. The complete CP fissure vein is not simply a universal synonym.

referenceFields.Course: From the cerebellomedullary/lateral recess region, emerges by the lateral aperture and curves around the floccular region into the ascending CPA component.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Fourth ventricular region and anterior tonsillar/fissural tributaries.
referenceFields.Outflow: Petrosal network or alternative CPA bridging outflow.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Fourth ventricle, lateral recess, foramen of Luschka and flocculus.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Neural/fissural course medial to the petrous bone. Keep the CPA segment clear of the petrous cortex until its dural connection.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Lateral recess; lateral aperture; flocculus; CPA collector Modelling interpretation Extend the existing cerebellopontine fissure segment medially. Preserve the hook and distinguish its components by location.
referenceFields.Variants: Passage relative to the flocculus and final outflow vary.
referenceFields.Naming: Sources partition the intraventricular, fissural and ascending components differently. The complete CP fissure vein is not simply a universal synonym.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I12, I13. I12 shows the ascending CPA component; I13 correlates cerebellomedullary, floccular and CPA parts
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S05. Bradac p. 148; Neuroangio lateral recess MRI. Existing IDs: vein.cerebellopontine_fissure.left, vein.cerebellopontine_fissure.right

structures.name: Veins of the superior cerebellar peduncles, right
aliases: Brachial tributaries of the precentral vein
structures.description: Runs over the superior cerebellar peduncles and converges towards the midline precentral vein.
structures.notes: Brachial is used for more than one peduncular segment; qualify the tributary.

referenceFields.Course: Runs over the superior cerebellar peduncles and converges towards the midline precentral vein.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Superior peduncular and adjacent cerebellar tributaries.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Superior cerebellar peduncles and upper fourth ventricular roof.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Superior cerebellar peduncles; lingula; precentral junction Modelling interpretation Add the paired converging limbs around the upper roof rather than lengthening the midline precentral tube.
referenceFields.Variants: May connect laterally rather than forming a single midline stem.
referenceFields.Naming: Brachial is used for more than one peduncular segment; qualify the tributary.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I15, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S06. Bradac p. 145; Neuroangio precentral/brachial examples.
referenceFields.Alternate names: Brachial tributaries of the precentral vein

structures.name: Vein of the middle cerebellar peduncle, right
structures.description: Ascends on the middle cerebellar peduncle from the lower CPA/pontomedullary region to petrosal or CP fissure collectors.
structures.notes: Usage varies. Do not equate every lateral pontine channel with the CP fissure collector.

referenceFields.Course: Ascends on the middle cerebellar peduncle from the lower CPA/pontomedullary region to petrosal or CP fissure collectors.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Lateral pontine and lateral medullary/fissural tributaries.
referenceFields.Outflow: Petrosal vein or cerebellopontine fissure collector.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Middle cerebellar peduncle, lateral pons and floccular vicinity.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Middle cerebellar peduncle; flocculus; lateral pons; petrosal junction Modelling interpretation Maintain a distinct surface course from P05 and review the lower existing lateral mesencephalic route for overlap.
referenceFields.Variants: May share a short terminal stem with fissural or transverse veins.
referenceFields.Naming: Usage varies. Do not equate every lateral pontine channel with the CP fissure collector.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I13, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S05, S07. Bradac pp. 144-148; Neuroangio lateral recess/lateral pontine distinction.

structures.name: Inferior vermian tonsillar collecting segment, right
structures.description: Curves around upper and lower posterior tonsillar margins and converges on the inferior vermian collector.
structures.notes: Two components in one family record; neither is simply an alias of the entire inferior vermian vein.

structures.name: Tonsillar surface veins, right
structures.description: Follows medial/lateral tonsillar surfaces towards inferior vermian or lateral recess collectors.
structures.notes: Medial, lateral and anterior/superior labels describe components with variable naming.

referenceFields.Course: Follows medial/lateral tonsillar surfaces towards inferior vermian or lateral recess collectors.
referenceFields.Outflow: Inferior vermian and lateral recess/fissural systems.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Cerebellar tonsils beside the medulla and lower fourth ventricle.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Above/within the foramen magnum region but on neural surfaces; do not follow the foramen rim.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Tonsil surfaces; inferior vermian vein; lateral recess Modelling interpretation Author distinct surface tributaries. Use the tonsil mesh to prevent a tube being placed through the tonsil.
referenceFields.Variants: Territory shifts between vermian and lateral recess outflow.
referenceFields.Naming: Medial, lateral and anterior/superior labels describe components with variable naming.

structures.name: Medial supratonsillar vein, right
structures.description: Courses at the medial/lateral margins of the inferior medullary velum above the tonsil.
structures.notes: The name alone can misleadingly imply tonsillar-surface drainage. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: Courses at the medial/lateral margins of the inferior medullary velum above the tonsil.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Inferior medullary velum and superior tonsillar region.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Inferior medullary velum; superior tonsil pole; dentate region Modelling interpretation Use the fissural roof as the anchor; this is not another posterior tonsillar surface loop.
referenceFields.Variants: Fine branches and alternative junctions require an exemplar.
referenceFields.Naming: The name alone can misleadingly imply tonsillar-surface drainage.
referenceFields.Evidence: Dissection topology supported; direct MRI course not curated
referenceFields.Images: I03, I23. General posterior fossa context only
referenceFields.Sources: S13. Matsushima Fig. 11 and Table 2.

structures.name: Dentate venous tributaries, right
structures.description: From the dentate region into supratonsillar/cerebellomedullary drainage.
structures.notes: Family record rather than a reliably visible single angiographic trunk. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: From the dentate region into supratonsillar/cerebellomedullary drainage.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Dentate nucleus and cerebellar white matter.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Dentate nucleus; deep cerebellar white matter; receiving fissural collector Modelling interpretation Obtain registered deep nuclei before drawing representative intraparenchymal tributaries.
referenceFields.Variants: Fine channels with variable visibility.
referenceFields.Naming: Family record rather than a reliably visible single angiographic trunk.

structures.name: Fourth ventricular choroidal veins, right
structures.description: Short plexus/tela channels into cerebellomedullary or inferior-peduncular collectors.
structures.notes: Distinct from supratentorial superior/inferior choroidal veins. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: Short plexus/tela channels into cerebellomedullary or inferior-peduncular collectors.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Fourth ventricular choroid plexus and tela choroidea.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Tela, lateral recess choroid plexus and lower ventricular roof.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Tela choroidea; choroid plexus; lateral recess Modelling interpretation Build only after the fourth ventricle and plexus are registered. Treat as optional fine anatomy.
referenceFields.Variants: Usually below conventional angiographic resolution.
referenceFields.Naming: Distinct from supratentorial superior/inferior choroidal veins.
referenceFields.Evidence: Drainage supported; detailed centreline unresolved
referenceFields.Images: I13. Lateral recess context, not direct depiction of the tiny choroidal tributaries
referenceFields.Sources: S05, S13. Neuroangio fourth ventricular veins; Matsushima Fig. 11.

structures.name: Lateral medullary veins, right
structures.description: Runs along the lateral/posterolateral medulla and connects rostrally with lateral pontine/peduncular drainage.
structures.notes: Lateral medullary is broader than the retro-olivary sulcal component.

referenceFields.Course: Runs along the lateral/posterolateral medulla and connects rostrally with lateral pontine/peduncular drainage.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Lateral medulla and connected transverse/fissural tributaries.
referenceFields.Outflow: Lateral pontine/petrosal and posterior medullary connections.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Lateral medullary surface.

referenceFields.Required landmarks: Medulla; olive; inferior cerebellar peduncle; pontomedullary junction Modelling interpretation Keep this posterior/lateral to the preolivary route and connect it to appropriate lower CPA collectors.

structures.notes: Do not use preolivary as an alternate name.

referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Retro-olivary sulcus and posterior olive margin.

structures.name: Preolivary veins, right
structures.description: Follows the preolivary sulcus with a superior pontomedullary connection.
structures.notes: Preolivary and retro-olivary refer to opposite olive margins. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: Follows the preolivary sulcus with a superior pontomedullary connection.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Between medullary pyramid and olive; beside CN XII rootlets.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Intracisternal on the medulla. Proximity to the hypoglossal canal does not imply a canal course.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Pyramid; olive; preolivary sulcus; CN XII rootlets Modelling interpretation Requires a correctly oriented olive/pyramid surface. Keep separate from the median anterior medullary vein and P15.

referenceFields.Naming: Preolivary and retro-olivary refer to opposite olive margins.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed

referenceFields.Course: Courses at the medial/lateral margins of the inferior medullary velum above the tonsil.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Inferior medullary velum and superior tonsillar region.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Inferior medullary velum; superior tonsil pole; dentate region Modelling interpretation Use the fissural roof as the anchor; this is not another posterior tonsillar surface loop.
referenceFields.Variants: Fine branches and alternative junctions require an exemplar.
referenceFields.Naming: The name alone can misleadingly imply tonsillar-surface drainage.
referenceFields.Evidence: Dissection topology supported; direct MRI course not curated
referenceFields.Images: I03, I23. General posterior fossa context only
referenceFields.Sources: S13. Matsushima Fig. 11 and Table 2.

structures.name: Dentate venous tributaries, left
structures.description: From the dentate region into supratonsillar/cerebellomedullary drainage.
structures.notes: Family record rather than a reliably visible single angiographic trunk. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: From the dentate region into supratonsillar/cerebellomedullary drainage.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Dentate nucleus and cerebellar white matter.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Dentate nucleus; deep cerebellar white matter; receiving fissural collector Modelling interpretation Obtain registered deep nuclei before drawing representative intraparenchymal tributaries.
referenceFields.Variants: Fine channels with variable visibility.
referenceFields.Naming: Family record rather than a reliably visible single angiographic trunk.
referenceFields.Evidence: Anatomical drainage supported; detailed centreline unresolved
referenceFields.Images: I03, I23. General context; no dedicated dentate vein image curated
referenceFields.Sources: S05, S13. Neuroangio fourth ventricular veins; Matsushima Table 2.

structures.name: Fourth ventricular choroidal veins, left
structures.description: Short plexus/tela channels into cerebellomedullary or inferior-peduncular collectors.
structures.notes: Distinct from supratentorial superior/inferior choroidal veins. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: Short plexus/tela channels into cerebellomedullary or inferior-peduncular collectors.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Fourth ventricular choroid plexus and tela choroidea.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Tela, lateral recess choroid plexus and lower ventricular roof.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Tela choroidea; choroid plexus; lateral recess Modelling interpretation Build only after the fourth ventricle and plexus are registered. Treat as optional fine anatomy.
referenceFields.Variants: Usually below conventional angiographic resolution.
referenceFields.Naming: Distinct from supratentorial superior/inferior choroidal veins.
referenceFields.Evidence: Drainage supported; detailed centreline unresolved
referenceFields.Images: I13. Lateral recess context, not direct depiction of the tiny choroidal tributaries
referenceFields.Sources: S05, S13. Neuroangio fourth ventricular veins; Matsushima Fig. 11.

structures.name: Lateral medullary veins, left
structures.description: Runs along the lateral/posterolateral medulla and connects rostrally with lateral pontine/peduncular drainage.
structures.notes: Lateral medullary is broader than the retro-olivary sulcal component.

referenceFields.Course: Runs along the lateral/posterolateral medulla and connects rostrally with lateral pontine/peduncular drainage.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Lateral medulla and connected transverse/fissural tributaries.
referenceFields.Outflow: Lateral pontine/petrosal and posterior medullary connections.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Lateral medullary surface.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Medulla; olive; inferior cerebellar peduncle; pontomedullary junction Modelling interpretation Keep this posterior/lateral to the preolivary route and connect it to appropriate lower CPA collectors.
referenceFields.Variants: May be small when anterior longitudinal channels dominate.
referenceFields.Naming: Lateral medullary is broader than the retro-olivary sulcal component.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I18, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S08. Bradac p. 144 and Fig. 9.16.

structures.name: Retro-olivary veins, left
structures.description: Runs behind the olive towards lateral medullary drainage.
structures.notes: Do not use preolivary as an alternate name.

referenceFields.Course: Runs behind the olive towards lateral medullary drainage.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Retro-olivary sulcus and posterior olive margin.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Olive; retro-olivary sulcus; lateral medullary collector Modelling interpretation Place behind the olive, separate from the preolivary vein in P17.
referenceFields.Variants: Often fine and asymmetric.
referenceFields.Naming: Do not use preolivary as an alternate name.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I18. Direct labelled MRI example
referenceFields.Sources: S08, S13. Neuroangio retro-olivary MRI; Matsushima Fig. 12.

structures.name: Preolivary veins, left
structures.description: Follows the preolivary sulcus with a superior pontomedullary connection.
structures.notes: Preolivary and retro-olivary refer to opposite olive margins. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: Follows the preolivary sulcus with a superior pontomedullary connection.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Between medullary pyramid and olive; beside CN XII rootlets.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Intracisternal on the medulla. Proximity to the hypoglossal canal does not imply a canal course.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Pyramid; olive; preolivary sulcus; CN XII rootlets Modelling interpretation Requires a correctly oriented olive/pyramid surface. Keep separate from the median anterior medullary vein and P15.
referenceFields.Variants: May be discontinuous.
referenceFields.Naming: Preolivary and retro-olivary refer to opposite olive margins.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I18. Olive/anterior medullary orientation only; the labelled retro-olivary vein is a different vessel
referenceFields.Sources: S12, S13. TA A12.3.06.050; Matsushima Fig. 12.
referenceFields.Alternate names: Lateral anterior medullary vein; Anterolateral medullary vein

structures.name: Veins of the inferior cerebellar peduncles, left
structures.description: Follows the restiform body between posterior median medullary and lateral/pontomedullary drainage.
structures.notes: Older marginal terminology is source-specific and does not refer to the dural marginal sinus. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: Follows the restiform body between posterior median medullary and lateral/pontomedullary drainage.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Posterior/lateral medullary and lower fourth ventricular region.
referenceFields.Outflow: Lateral medullary/pontomedullary and posterior median pathways.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Inferior cerebellar peduncle and lower fourth ventricle.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Restiform body; obex; lower fourth ventricle; lateral medulla Modelling interpretation Requires a registered inferior peduncle and obex. Distinguish it from the tonsillar outline and the lateral recess hook.
referenceFields.Variants: Terminal connections and dominance vary.
referenceFields.Naming: Older marginal terminology is source-specific and does not refer to the dural marginal sinus.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I23. General topology only; a dedicated inferior-peduncular cross-sectional exemplar is still needed
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S13. Bradac p. 144; Matsushima Fig. 11.
referenceFields.Alternate names: Vein of restiform body; Marginal vein of fourth ventricle

structures.name: Lateral posterior medullary veins, left
structures.description: Runs on the dorsolateral medulla near the inferior cerebellar peduncle.
structures.notes: Do not generate a second identical lateral-medullary tube solely from the label. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: Runs on the dorsolateral medulla near the inferior cerebellar peduncle.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Posterior-lateral medulla and restiform body.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Dorsolateral medulla; inferior cerebellar peduncle Modelling interpretation Resolve the distinction from the lateral medullary collector using a dissection or registered MRI exemplar.
referenceFields.Variants: Small distributed channels.
referenceFields.Naming: Do not generate a second identical lateral-medullary tube solely from the label.
referenceFields.Evidence: Named region supported; representative course needs further imaging
referenceFields.Images: I03, I23. General context only
referenceFields.Sources: S12, S13. TA A12.3.06.052; Matsushima Fig. 11.

structures.name: Lateral anterior pontomesencephalic veins, left
structures.description: Follows anterolateral brainstem, linking nearby peduncular, transverse pontine and pontomedullary channels.
structures.notes: Distinct from lateral mesencephalic anatomy.

referenceFields.Course: Follows anterolateral brainstem, linking nearby peduncular, transverse pontine and pontomedullary channels.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Anterolateral pons and midbrain, away from the median basilar sulcus.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the prepontine/interpeduncular cisternal space; not a vein on the clivus.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Anterior pons; midbrain; basilar sulcus; transverse connectors Modelling interpretation Add a partial asymmetric channel. Do not automatically duplicate the full existing median conduit on both sides.
referenceFields.Variants: Rarely a complete uninterrupted midbrain-to-lower-pons channel.
referenceFields.Naming: Distinct from lateral mesencephalic anatomy.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I20, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S08, S13. Bradac pp. 143-144 and Fig. 9.9; Matsushima Fig. 12.

structures.name: Vein of the pontomesencephalic sulcus, left
structures.description: Follows the sulcus at the upper border of the pons.
structures.notes: Neuroangio sometimes groups this with transverse pontine; Rhoton distinguishes anatomical levels.

referenceFields.Course: Follows the sulcus at the upper border of the pons.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Pontomesencephalic junction.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Upper pontine border; midbrain; anterior and lateral channels Modelling interpretation Check the height of the existing transverse pontine route. Create a second channel only if it represents a distinct sulcal level.
referenceFields.Variants: May be short or incomplete.
referenceFields.Naming: Neuroangio sometimes groups this with transverse pontine; Rhoton distinguishes anatomical levels.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S04, S13. Neuroangio transverse brainstem discussion; Matsushima Fig. 12. Existing IDs: vein.transverse_pontine.left, vein.transverse_pontine.right

structures.name: Transverse medullary veins, left
structures.description: Short transverse segments over medullary pyramids or olives.
structures.notes: Distinct level from the existing pontomedullary sulcus veins.

referenceFields.Course: Short transverse segments over medullary pyramids or olives.
referenceFields.Outflow: Median, preolivary and lateral medullary network.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Medullary surface at one or more levels.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Pyramids; olives; anterior medullary vein; lateral medullary vein Modelling interpretation Use one or two unequal short connections. Do not make a complete regular ring around the medulla.
referenceFields.Variants: Partial and asymmetric channels.
referenceFields.Naming: Distinct level from the existing pontomedullary sulcus veins.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I18, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S12, S13. Bradac p. 144; TA A12.3.06.051; Matsushima Fig. 12.

structures.name: Cerebral peduncular veins, left
structures.description: Runs laterally from the interpeduncular region around the cerebral peduncle towards the basal vein.
structures.notes: Cerebral peduncular veins are different from superior/middle/inferior cerebellar peduncular veins.

referenceFields.Course: Runs laterally from the interpeduncular region around the cerebral peduncle towards the basal vein.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Inferior thalamic and anterior midbrain tributaries.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Interpeduncular fossa and cerebral peduncle.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Intracisternal above the clivus and near the tentorial incisura; no direct skull attachment.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Interpeduncular fossa; cerebral peduncle; basal vein; posterior communicating vein Modelling interpretation Inspect whether the anterior existing basal course already represents part of this segment before adding a parallel tube.
referenceFields.Variants: Connected across the midline by the posterior communicating vein.
referenceFields.Naming: Cerebral peduncular veins are different from superior/middle/inferior cerebellar peduncular veins.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I01, I03, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels

structures.name: Tectal and intercollicular veins, left
structures.description: Courses over the collicular/tectal surface towards the precentral/superior vermian or adjacent Galenic system.
structures.notes: Intercollicular is a specific location/component within the tectal family, not an alias for every tectal vein.

referenceFields.Course: Courses over the collicular/tectal surface towards the precentral/superior vermian or adjacent Galenic system.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Superior and inferior colliculi and quadrigeminal cistern.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Colliculi; tectal surface; quadrigeminal cistern Modelling interpretation Author a small surface representative after registering the tectum. Keep it anterior to the cerebellar surface and distinct from precentral.
referenceFields.Variants: Number and terminal connections vary.
referenceFields.Naming: Intercollicular is a specific location/component within the tectal family, not an alias for every tectal vein.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I16. Labelled collicular example; neighbouring culmen veins are separate
referenceFields.Sources: S06, S12. Neuroangio high-field collicular image; TA A12.3.06.041.

structures.name: Upper cervical foraminal venous connection, left
structures.description: Passes from anterior/posterior cervical perimedullary channels towards radicular and neural foraminal venous networks.
structures.notes: Radicular, foraminal and dural bridging portions need separate anatomical labels where shown. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: Passes from anterior/posterior cervical perimedullary channels towards radicular and neural foraminal venous networks.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Upper cervical cord and nerve root corridors.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Exit follows a nerve root/foraminal corridor at the chosen level; no arbitrary canal through the atlas or occiput.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Upper cervical cord; nerve root corridor; C1-C2 foraminal anatomy Modelling interpretation Connect the existing anterior spinal course and proposed dorsal course to a short representative exit route.
referenceFields.Variants: Level and direction vary; prominent cervical outflow is a variant.
referenceFields.Naming: Radicular, foraminal and dural bridging portions need separate anatomical labels where shown.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I10. Angiographic variant showing cervical exit routes
referenceFields.Sources: S04, S08. Neuroangio cervical outflow examples. Existing IDs: vein.anterior_spinal

structures.name: Upper cervical radicular vein, left
structures.description: Passes from anterior/posterior cervical perimedullary channels towards radicular and neural foraminal venous networks.
structures.notes: Radicular, foraminal and dural bridging portions need separate anatomical labels where shown. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: Passes from anterior/posterior cervical perimedullary channels towards radicular and neural foraminal venous networks.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Upper cervical cord and nerve root corridors.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Exit follows a nerve root/foraminal corridor at the chosen level; no arbitrary canal through the atlas or occiput.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Upper cervical cord; nerve root corridor; C1-C2 foraminal anatomy Modelling interpretation Connect the existing anterior spinal course and proposed dorsal course to a short representative exit route.
referenceFields.Variants: Level and direction vary; prominent cervical outflow is a variant.
referenceFields.Naming: Radicular, foraminal and dural bridging portions need separate anatomical labels where shown.

referenceFields.Sources: S04, S08. Neuroangio cervical outflow examples. Existing IDs: vein.anterior_spinal

structures.name: Posterior mesencephalic vein, right
structures.description: May have a long course from the interpeduncular region or form only a posterior continuation of lateral mesencephalic drainage to Galen.
structures.notes: Accessory basal vein is an interpretation when an additional basal-like channel coexists; not an unconditional synonym.

referenceFields.Course: May have a long course from the interpeduncular region or form only a posterior continuation of lateral mesencephalic drainage to Galen.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Midbrain surface and quadrigeminal cistern.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: No direct bony attachment. Position is set by ventricular or cisternal anatomy, rather than a skull groove.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Midbrain; lateral mesencephalic vein; basal vein; Galen Modelling interpretation Choose a documented variant and compare with the existing basal centreline. Do not always add a complete extra basal-like vessel.
referenceFields.Variants: Can replace part of the basal vein or coexist with it.
referenceFields.Naming: Accessory basal vein is an interpretation when an additional basal-like channel coexists; not an unconditional synonym.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I03, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
referenceFields.Sources: S01. Bradac pp. 137-138 and Figs. 9.14-9.16.

structures.name: Prepontine bridging veins, right
structures.description: Crosses the prepontine cistern from anterior brainstem channels to a posterior cavernous or clival dural endpoint.
structures.notes: A group of channels rather than one invariant named vein.

referenceFields.Course: Crosses the prepontine cistern from anterior brainstem channels to a posterior cavernous or clival dural endpoint.
referenceFields.Outflow: Posterior cavernous sinus or clival/basilar plexus.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Anterior pons and prepontine cistern.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: The terminal dural channel relates to posterior parasellar/clival dura. The bridging segment is suspended in cisternal space.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Anterior pons; prepontine cistern; posterior cavernous/clival endpoint Modelling interpretation Attach locally to a verified dural endpoint. Do not extend the cavernous sinus body to envelop this entire vein.
referenceFields.Variants: Unilateral, bilateral or asymmetric; balances with petrosal outflow.
referenceFields.Naming: A group of channels rather than one invariant named vein.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I20. Direct MRI and angiographic examples
referenceFields.Sources: S01, S09. Bradac pp. 144 and 147; Neuroangio prepontine bridging examples.

structures.name: CPA bridging veins to the inferior petrosal sinus, left
structures.description: Crosses from the lower CPA/fissural network towards the inferior petrosal sinus.
structures.notes: Inferior petrosal vein is a bridging vessel; inferior petrosal sinus is the dural channel.

referenceFields.Course: Crosses from the lower CPA/fissural network towards the inferior petrosal sinus.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Lateral recess and adjacent lateral brainstem collectors.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Lower CPA, lateral pons/medulla and lateral recess network.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Endpoint at inferior petrosal drainage along the petroclival/petro-occipital region; distinct from superior petrosal entry at the petrous ridge.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: CPA collector; inferior petrosal sinus; petrous apex/clival junction Modelling interpretation Author an alternative endpoint to the lower IPS. Avoid connecting every CPA tributary to the superior petrosal vein.
referenceFields.Variants: May coexist with or replace usual superior petrosal drainage.
referenceFields.Naming: Inferior petrosal vein is a bridging vessel; inferior petrosal sinus is the dural channel.
referenceFields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
referenceFields.Images: I13, I21. Direct alternative-outflow example; use source arrows
referenceFields.Sources: S05, S09. Neuroangio lateral recess and bridging examples.

structures.name: Lower brainstem bridging vein to marginal sinus, right
structures.description: Passes through a lower cranial nerve corridor to jugular, sigmoid, inferior petrosal or marginal dural drainage.
structures.notes: Vagal is a route-specific name; not an alias for all lower brainstem bridges. Fine regional placement is illustrative. The atlas does not resolve every sulcus, nucleus, velum, rootlet or nerve corridor; these landmarks require anatomical review.

referenceFields.Course: Passes through a lower cranial nerve corridor to jugular, sigmoid, inferior petrosal or marginal dural drainage.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Lower CPA, lateral medulla and lower cranial nerve corridors.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Endpoint-specific relation to jugular bulb/sigmoid groove or foramen magnum dura; no universal bony course.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Lateral medulla; lower cranial nerve corridor; chosen dural endpoint Modelling interpretation Implement one documented route at a time. Confirm the actual target rather than extending a generic straight bridge through bone.
referenceFields.Variants: Different channels have different dural targets.
referenceFields.Naming: Vagal is a route-specific name; not an alias for all lower brainstem bridges.
referenceFields.Evidence: Group topology supported; exemplar needed for the selected dural target
referenceFields.Images: I03, I21, I23. General orientation; I21 mainly demonstrates inferior petrosal drainage
referenceFields.Sources: S13. Matsushima Figs. 11-13 and other bridging veins discussion.

referenceFields.Naming: Intercollicular is a specific location/component within the tectal family, not an alias for every tectal vein.

structures.name: Pontotrigeminal vein, right
structures.description: Links superior/middle peduncular territory with petrosal drainage and lateral mesencephalic connections.
structures.notes: Lower existing lateral mesencephalic-to-petrosal component relabelled at the upper pontine level. Original course retained with local ostia and topology repair; named boundary is a teaching convention and requires review.

referenceFields.Course: Links superior/middle peduncular territory with petrosal drainage and lateral mesencephalic connections.
referenceFields.Tributaries: Peduncular and connected lateral mesencephalic tributaries.
referenceFields.Parenchymal relations: Peduncular surface and trigeminal region.
referenceFields.Bone and dura: Intracisternal near the petrous face; reaches dura only through the petrosal terminal connection.
referenceFields.Required landmarks: Peduncular surface; CN V region; lateral mesencephalic vein; petrosal vein Modelling interpretation Our existing lateral mesencephalic-to-petrosal course may already cover its lower component. Audit and label that segment before adding geometry.
referenceFields.Variants: Can be developed separately from the upper lateral mesencephalic segment.
referenceFields.Naming: Do not use pontotrigeminal as a synonym for the whole lateral mesencephalic vein.

referenceFields.Images: I17. Direct angiographic comparison of upper H and lower G components

structures.description: Links superior/middle peduncular territory with petrosal drainage and lateral mesencephalic connections.
structures.notes: Lower existing lateral mesencephalic-to-petrosal component relabelled at the upper pontine level. Original course retained with local ostia and topology repair; named boundary is a teaching convention and requires review.

fields.Course: Courses over superior hemispheric folia towards Galenic/vermians, petrosal collectors or a tentorial/transverse endpoint.
fields.Outflow: Galenic, petrosal or tentorial/transverse groups, depending on location.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Superior cerebellar hemisphere beneath the tentorium.
fields.Bone and dura: The pial segment follows cerebellum. A bridging terminal segment reaches tentorial dura or a sinus; only that endpoint is dural.
fields.Required landmarks: Superior cerebellar surface; tentorium; selected sinus endpoint Modelling interpretation Add a medial and a lateral representative with different outflow options. Avoid forcing every superior vein through the superior vermian trunk.
fields.Variants: Relative dominance varies markedly.
fields.Naming: Family record; named trunks vary.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I07, I11, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S04. Bradac pp. 145-148; Neuroangio cerebellar surfaces.

fields.Course: Converges across the anterior cerebellar surface towards fissural and petrosal collectors.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Petrosal cerebellar surface beside the middle cerebellar peduncle.
fields.Bone and dura: Faces the posterior petrous surface, but lies on cerebellum rather than plastered against bone.
fields.Required landmarks: Anterior cerebellar surface; middle cerebellar peduncle; petrosal collector Modelling interpretation Use superior and inferior surface representatives feeding the existing fissure/petrosal trunks.
fields.Variants: Can dominate cerebellar outflow.
fields.Naming: Do not confuse these surface tributaries with the short petrosal bridging trunk.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I07, I08. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S04. Bradac p. 148; Neuroangio anterior surface dominance.
