fields.Course: Follows the horizontal fissural region on the anterior/lateral cerebellum towards the petrosal network.
fields.Tributaries: Superior and inferior anterior cerebellar tributaries.
fields.Outflow: Petrosal vein and related fissural collectors.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Great horizontal fissure and anterior cerebellar hemisphere.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Horizontal fissure; anterior cerebellar surface; petrosal junction Modelling interpretation Reconcile the course with the existing cerebellopontine fissure vein before creating an overlapping trunk.
fields.Variants: Size and connections vary.
fields.Naming: Anterior cerebellar vein can be used more broadly; bind the alias to the documented course.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I21, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S09. Bradac pp. 144 and 148; Neuroangio bridging/horizontal fissure example.
fields.Alternate names: Anterior cerebellar vein; Vein of horizontal cerebellar fissure

fields.Course: Runs over the inferior/posterior cerebellar surface to direct transverse/sigmoid or short tentorial drainage.
fields.Outflow: Transverse or sigmoid sinus, with variable tentorial and vermian connections.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Posteroinferior cerebellar surface.
fields.Bone and dura: Remote from the occipital inner table until the terminal bridging segment reaches the transverse/sigmoid dural region.
fields.Required landmarks: Inferior cerebellar surface; transverse groove; sigmoid groove Modelling interpretation Keep the existing veins but add representative direct dural outflow; revise the current sole inferior-vermian connection.
fields.Variants: Can substitute for a small inferior vermian group.
fields.Naming: Extension of current anatomy, not a wholly missing family.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I07. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S04. Bradac p. 148; Neuroangio inferior surface examples. Existing IDs: vein.inferior_hemispheric.left, vein.inferior_hemispheric.right

P05.name: Vein of the lateral recess of the fourth ventricle

fields.Course: From the cerebellomedullary/lateral recess region, emerges by the lateral aperture and curves around the floccular region into the ascending CPA component.
fields.Tributaries: Fourth ventricular region and anterior tonsillar/fissural tributaries.
fields.Outflow: Petrosal network or alternative CPA bridging outflow.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Fourth ventricle, lateral recess, foramen of Luschka and flocculus.
fields.Bone and dura: Neural/fissural course medial to the petrous bone. Keep the CPA segment clear of the petrous cortex until its dural connection.
fields.Required landmarks: Lateral recess; lateral aperture; flocculus; CPA collector Modelling interpretation Extend the existing cerebellopontine fissure segment medially. Preserve the hook and distinguish its components by location.
fields.Variants: Passage relative to the flocculus and final outflow vary.
fields.Naming: Sources partition the intraventricular, fissural and ascending components differently. The complete CP fissure vein is not simply a universal synonym.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I12, I13. I12 shows the ascending CPA component; I13 correlates cerebellomedullary, floccular and CPA parts
fields.Sources: S01, S05. Bradac p. 148; Neuroangio lateral recess MRI. Existing IDs: vein.cerebellopontine_fissure.left, vein.cerebellopontine_fissure.right

P06.name: Veins of the superior cerebellar peduncles

fields.Course: Runs over the superior cerebellar peduncles and converges towards the midline precentral vein.
fields.Tributaries: Superior peduncular and adjacent cerebellar tributaries.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Superior cerebellar peduncles and upper fourth ventricular roof.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Superior cerebellar peduncles; lingula; precentral junction Modelling interpretation Add the paired converging limbs around the upper roof rather than lengthening the midline precentral tube.
fields.Variants: May connect laterally rather than forming a single midline stem.
fields.Naming: Brachial is used for more than one peduncular segment; qualify the tributary.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I15, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S06. Bradac p. 145; Neuroangio precentral/brachial examples.
fields.Alternate names: Brachial tributaries of the precentral vein

P07.name: Vein of the middle cerebellar peduncle

fields.Course: Ascends on the middle cerebellar peduncle from the lower CPA/pontomedullary region to petrosal or CP fissure collectors.
fields.Tributaries: Lateral pontine and lateral medullary/fissural tributaries.
fields.Outflow: Petrosal vein or cerebellopontine fissure collector.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Middle cerebellar peduncle, lateral pons and floccular vicinity.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Middle cerebellar peduncle; flocculus; lateral pons; petrosal junction Modelling interpretation Maintain a distinct surface course from P05 and review the lower existing lateral mesencephalic route for overlap.
fields.Variants: May share a short terminal stem with fissural or transverse veins.
fields.Naming: Usage varies. Do not equate every lateral pontine channel with the CP fissure collector.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I13, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S05, S07. Bradac pp. 144-148; Neuroangio lateral recess/lateral pontine distinction.

P08.name: Veins of the inferior cerebellar peduncles

fields.Course: Follows the restiform body between posterior median medullary and lateral/pontomedullary drainage.
fields.Tributaries: Posterior/lateral medullary and lower fourth ventricular region.
fields.Outflow: Lateral medullary/pontomedullary and posterior median pathways.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Inferior cerebellar peduncle and lower fourth ventricle.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Restiform body; obex; lower fourth ventricle; lateral medulla Modelling interpretation Requires a registered inferior peduncle and obex. Distinguish it from the tonsillar outline and the lateral recess hook.
fields.Variants: Terminal connections and dominance vary.
fields.Naming: Older marginal terminology is source-specific and does not refer to the dural marginal sinus.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I23. General topology only; a dedicated inferior-peduncular cross-sectional exemplar is still needed
fields.Sources: S01, S13. Bradac p. 144; Matsushima Fig. 11.
fields.Alternate names: Vein of restiform body; Marginal vein of fourth ventricle

fields.Course: Follows medial/lateral tonsillar surfaces towards inferior vermian or lateral recess collectors.
fields.Outflow: Inferior vermian and lateral recess/fissural systems.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Cerebellar tonsils beside the medulla and lower fourth ventricle.
fields.Bone and dura: Above/within the foramen magnum region but on neural surfaces; do not follow the foramen rim.
fields.Required landmarks: Tonsil surfaces; inferior vermian vein; lateral recess Modelling interpretation Author distinct surface tributaries. Use the tonsil mesh to prevent a tube being placed through the tonsil.
fields.Variants: Territory shifts between vermian and lateral recess outflow.
fields.Naming: Medial, lateral and anterior/superior labels describe components with variable naming.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I14, I21. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S05. Bradac Figs. 9.14-9.16; Neuroangio tonsillar section.

fields.Course: Curves around upper and lower posterior tonsillar margins and converges on the inferior vermian collector.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Posterior tonsil and inferior vermis.
fields.Bone and dura: Separate from the occipital bone and posterior foramen magnum rim; follows the tonsillar contours.
fields.Required landmarks: Posterior tonsil; superior and inferior tonsil poles; inferior vermian vein Modelling interpretation Add the two limbs of the tonsillar outline to the existing inferior vermian trunk.
fields.Variants: Asymmetric development and alternative fissural connections.
fields.Naming: Two components in one family record; neither is simply an alias of the entire inferior vermian vein.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I14. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S05. Bradac p. 148 and Fig. 9.16; Neuroangio retrotonsillar outline. Existing IDs: vein.inferior_vermian.left, vein.inferior_vermian.right

fields.Course: Courses at the medial/lateral margins of the inferior medullary velum above the tonsil.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Inferior medullary velum and superior tonsillar region.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Inferior medullary velum; superior tonsil pole; dentate region Modelling interpretation Use the fissural roof as the anchor; this is not another posterior tonsillar surface loop.
fields.Variants: Fine branches and alternative junctions require an exemplar.
fields.Naming: The name alone can misleadingly imply tonsillar-surface drainage.
fields.Evidence: Dissection topology supported; direct MRI course not curated
fields.Images: I03, I23. General posterior fossa context only
fields.Sources: S13. Matsushima Fig. 11 and Table 2.

fields.Course: From the dentate region into supratonsillar/cerebellomedullary drainage.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Dentate nucleus and cerebellar white matter.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Dentate nucleus; deep cerebellar white matter; receiving fissural collector Modelling interpretation Obtain registered deep nuclei before drawing representative intraparenchymal tributaries.
fields.Variants: Fine channels with variable visibility.
fields.Naming: Family record rather than a reliably visible single angiographic trunk.
fields.Evidence: Anatomical drainage supported; detailed centreline unresolved
fields.Images: I03, I23. General context; no dedicated dentate vein image curated
fields.Sources: S05, S13. Neuroangio fourth ventricular veins; Matsushima Table 2.

fields.Course: Short plexus/tela channels into cerebellomedullary or inferior-peduncular collectors.
fields.Tributaries: Fourth ventricular choroid plexus and tela choroidea.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Tela, lateral recess choroid plexus and lower ventricular roof.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Tela choroidea; choroid plexus; lateral recess Modelling interpretation Build only after the fourth ventricle and plexus are registered. Treat as optional fine anatomy.
fields.Variants: Usually below conventional angiographic resolution.
fields.Naming: Distinct from supratentorial superior/inferior choroidal veins.
fields.Evidence: Drainage supported; detailed centreline unresolved
fields.Images: I13. Lateral recess context, not direct depiction of the tiny choroidal tributaries
fields.Sources: S05, S13. Neuroangio fourth ventricular veins; Matsushima Fig. 11.

fields.Course: Runs along the lateral/posterolateral medulla and connects rostrally with lateral pontine/peduncular drainage.
fields.Tributaries: Lateral medulla and connected transverse/fissural tributaries.
fields.Outflow: Lateral pontine/petrosal and posterior medullary connections.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Lateral medullary surface.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Medulla; olive; inferior cerebellar peduncle; pontomedullary junction Modelling interpretation Keep this posterior/lateral to the preolivary route and connect it to appropriate lower CPA collectors.
fields.Variants: May be small when anterior longitudinal channels dominate.
fields.Naming: Lateral medullary is broader than the retro-olivary sulcal component.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I18, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S08. Bradac p. 144 and Fig. 9.16.

fields.Course: Runs behind the olive towards lateral medullary drainage.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Retro-olivary sulcus and posterior olive margin.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Olive; retro-olivary sulcus; lateral medullary collector Modelling interpretation Place behind the olive, separate from the preolivary vein in P17.
fields.Variants: Often fine and asymmetric.
fields.Naming: Do not use preolivary as an alternate name.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I18. Direct labelled MRI example
fields.Sources: S08, S13. Neuroangio retro-olivary MRI; Matsushima Fig. 12.

fields.Course: Follows anterolateral brainstem, linking nearby peduncular, transverse pontine and pontomedullary channels.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Anterolateral pons and midbrain, away from the median basilar sulcus.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the prepontine/interpeduncular cisternal space; not a vein on the clivus.
fields.Required landmarks: Anterior pons; midbrain; basilar sulcus; transverse connectors Modelling interpretation Add a partial asymmetric channel. Do not automatically duplicate the full existing median conduit on both sides.
fields.Variants: Rarely a complete uninterrupted midbrain-to-lower-pons channel.
fields.Naming: Distinct from lateral mesencephalic anatomy.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I20, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S08, S13. Bradac pp. 143-144 and Fig. 9.9; Matsushima Fig. 12.

fields.Course: Follows the preolivary sulcus with a superior pontomedullary connection.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Between medullary pyramid and olive; beside CN XII rootlets.
fields.Bone and dura: Intracisternal on the medulla. Proximity to the hypoglossal canal does not imply a canal course.
fields.Required landmarks: Pyramid; olive; preolivary sulcus; CN XII rootlets Modelling interpretation Requires a correctly oriented olive/pyramid surface. Keep separate from the median anterior medullary vein and P15.
fields.Variants: May be discontinuous.
fields.Naming: Preolivary and retro-olivary refer to opposite olive margins.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I18. Olive/anterior medullary orientation only; the labelled retro-olivary vein is a different vessel
fields.Sources: S12, S13. TA A12.3.06.050; Matsushima Fig. 12.
fields.Alternate names: Lateral anterior medullary vein; Anterolateral medullary vein

fields.Course: Forms from paired posterior/restiform-body channels and continues caudally as posterior spinal drainage.
fields.Outflow: Posterior spinal and connected lateral medullary network.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Posterior medulla and obex region.
fields.Bone and dura: Posterior to medulla inside the foramen magnum/cervical canal; clear of occipital bone and posterior atlas arch.
fields.Required landmarks: Obex; posterior medulla; posterior cord surface Modelling interpretation Add the caudal dorsal midline route and paired upper convergence. Avoid copying the ventral anterior spinal course.
fields.Variants: Continuity and size vary.
fields.Naming: Posterior/dorsal label depends on source.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I19, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Alternate names: Posteromedian medullary vein; Median dorsal medullary vein

fields.Course: Runs on the dorsolateral medulla near the inferior cerebellar peduncle.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Posterior-lateral medulla and restiform body.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Dorsolateral medulla; inferior cerebellar peduncle Modelling interpretation Resolve the distinction from the lateral medullary collector using a dissection or registered MRI exemplar.
fields.Variants: Small distributed channels.
fields.Naming: Do not generate a second identical lateral-medullary tube solely from the label.
fields.Evidence: Named region supported; representative course needs further imaging
fields.Images: I03, I23. General context only
fields.Sources: S12, S13. TA A12.3.06.052; Matsushima Fig. 11.

fields.Course: Descends on the posterior cervical cord surface from posterior medullary connections.
fields.Tributaries: Posterior cord and connected medullary/fissural channels.
fields.Outflow: Cervical perimedullary network and radicular/foraminal connections.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Dorsal cervical cord, posterior medulla and foramen magnum.
fields.Bone and dura: Inside the canal, anterior to the posterior atlas arch; not in the bony vertebral venous plexus itself.
fields.Required landmarks: Dorsal cord surface; foramen magnum; C1 posterior arch Modelling interpretation Limit the initial model to the craniovertebral segment. Add local radicular outflow without drawing an entire spinal system.
fields.Variants: Median and posterolateral forms and variable connections.
fields.Naming: These are components/arrangements of the dorsal spinal network, not universally interchangeable single-vessel names.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I10, I19. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S08. Bradac p. 144; Neuroangio posterior spinal MRI.
fields.Alternate names: Posterior median spinal vein; Posterolateral spinal veins

fields.Course: Runs laterally from the interpeduncular region around the cerebral peduncle towards the basal vein.
fields.Tributaries: Inferior thalamic and anterior midbrain tributaries.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Interpeduncular fossa and cerebral peduncle.
fields.Bone and dura: Intracisternal above the clivus and near the tentorial incisura; no direct skull attachment.
fields.Required landmarks: Interpeduncular fossa; cerebral peduncle; basal vein; posterior communicating vein Modelling interpretation Inspect whether the anterior existing basal course already represents part of this segment before adding a parallel tube.
fields.Variants: Connected across the midline by the posterior communicating vein.
fields.Naming: Cerebral peduncular veins are different from superior/middle/inferior cerebellar peduncular veins.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I01, I03, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels

fields.Course: Courses over the collicular/tectal surface towards the precentral/superior vermian or adjacent Galenic system.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Superior and inferior colliculi and quadrigeminal cistern.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Colliculi; tectal surface; quadrigeminal cistern Modelling interpretation Author a small surface representative after registering the tectum. Keep it anterior to the cerebellar surface and distinct from precentral.
fields.Variants: Number and terminal connections vary.
fields.Naming: Intercollicular is a specific location/component within the tectal family, not an alias for every tectal vein.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I16. Labelled collicular example; neighbouring culmen veins are separate
fields.Sources: S06, S12. Neuroangio high-field collicular image; TA A12.3.06.041.

fields.Course: May have a long course from the interpeduncular region or form only a posterior continuation of lateral mesencephalic drainage to Galen.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Midbrain surface and quadrigeminal cistern.
fields.Bone and dura: No direct bony attachment. Position is set by ventricular or cisternal anatomy, rather than a skull groove.
fields.Required landmarks: Midbrain; lateral mesencephalic vein; basal vein; Galen Modelling interpretation Choose a documented variant and compare with the existing basal centreline. Do not always add a complete extra basal-like vessel.
fields.Variants: Can replace part of the basal vein or coexist with it.
fields.Naming: Accessory basal vein is an interpretation when an additional basal-like channel coexists; not an unconditional synonym.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01. Bradac pp. 137-138 and Figs. 9.14-9.16.

fields.Course: Follows the sulcus at the upper border of the pons.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Pontomesencephalic junction.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Upper pontine border; midbrain; anterior and lateral channels Modelling interpretation Check the height of the existing transverse pontine route. Create a second channel only if it represents a distinct sulcal level.
fields.Variants: May be short or incomplete.
fields.Naming: Neuroangio sometimes groups this with transverse pontine; Rhoton distinguishes anatomical levels.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S04, S13. Neuroangio transverse brainstem discussion; Matsushima Fig. 12. Existing IDs: vein.transverse_pontine.left, vein.transverse_pontine.right

fields.Course: Short transverse segments over medullary pyramids or olives.
fields.Outflow: Median, preolivary and lateral medullary network.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Medullary surface at one or more levels.
fields.Bone and dura: Within the posterior cranial fossa. The neural surface sets the course; the enclosing skull is not a centreline anchor.
fields.Required landmarks: Pyramids; olives; anterior medullary vein; lateral medullary vein Modelling interpretation Use one or two unequal short connections. Do not make a complete regular ring around the medulla.
fields.Variants: Partial and asymmetric channels.
fields.Naming: Distinct level from the existing pontomedullary sulcus veins.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I03, I18, I23. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S12, S13. Bradac p. 144; TA A12.3.06.051; Matsushima Fig. 12.

fields.Course: Crosses the prepontine cistern from anterior brainstem channels to a posterior cavernous or clival dural endpoint.
fields.Outflow: Posterior cavernous sinus or clival/basilar plexus.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Anterior pons and prepontine cistern.
fields.Bone and dura: The terminal dural channel relates to posterior parasellar/clival dura. The bridging segment is suspended in cisternal space.
fields.Required landmarks: Anterior pons; prepontine cistern; posterior cavernous/clival endpoint Modelling interpretation Attach locally to a verified dural endpoint. Do not extend the cavernous sinus body to envelop this entire vein.
fields.Variants: Unilateral, bilateral or asymmetric; balances with petrosal outflow.
fields.Naming: A group of channels rather than one invariant named vein.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I20. Direct MRI and angiographic examples
fields.Sources: S01, S09. Bradac pp. 144 and 147; Neuroangio prepontine bridging examples.

P27.name: CPA bridging veins to the inferior petrosal sinus

fields.Course: Crosses from the lower CPA/fissural network towards the inferior petrosal sinus.
fields.Tributaries: Lateral recess and adjacent lateral brainstem collectors.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Lower CPA, lateral pons/medulla and lateral recess network.
fields.Bone and dura: Endpoint at inferior petrosal drainage along the petroclival/petro-occipital region; distinct from superior petrosal entry at the petrous ridge.
fields.Required landmarks: CPA collector; inferior petrosal sinus; petrous apex/clival junction Modelling interpretation Author an alternative endpoint to the lower IPS. Avoid connecting every CPA tributary to the superior petrosal vein.
fields.Variants: May coexist with or replace usual superior petrosal drainage.
fields.Naming: Inferior petrosal vein is a bridging vessel; inferior petrosal sinus is the dural channel.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I13, I21. Direct alternative-outflow example; use source arrows
fields.Sources: S05, S09. Neuroangio lateral recess and bridging examples.

fields.Course: Passes through a lower cranial nerve corridor to jugular, sigmoid, inferior petrosal or marginal dural drainage.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Lower CPA, lateral medulla and lower cranial nerve corridors.
fields.Bone and dura: Endpoint-specific relation to jugular bulb/sigmoid groove or foramen magnum dura; no universal bony course.
fields.Required landmarks: Lateral medulla; lower cranial nerve corridor; chosen dural endpoint Modelling interpretation Implement one documented route at a time. Confirm the actual target rather than extending a generic straight bridge through bone.
fields.Variants: Different channels have different dural targets.
fields.Naming: Vagal is a route-specific name; not an alias for all lower brainstem bridges.
fields.Evidence: Group topology supported; exemplar needed for the selected dural target
fields.Images: I03, I21, I23. General orientation; I21 mainly demonstrates inferior petrosal drainage
fields.Sources: S13. Matsushima Figs. 11-13 and other bridging veins discussion.

P29.name: Upper cervical radicular and foraminal venous connections

fields.Course: Passes from anterior/posterior cervical perimedullary channels towards radicular and neural foraminal venous networks.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Upper cervical cord and nerve root corridors.
fields.Bone and dura: Exit follows a nerve root/foraminal corridor at the chosen level; no arbitrary canal through the atlas or occiput.
fields.Required landmarks: Upper cervical cord; nerve root corridor; C1-C2 foraminal anatomy Modelling interpretation Connect the existing anterior spinal course and proposed dorsal course to a short representative exit route.
fields.Variants: Level and direction vary; prominent cervical outflow is a variant.
fields.Naming: Radicular, foraminal and dural bridging portions need separate anatomical labels where shown.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I10. Angiographic variant showing cervical exit routes
fields.Sources: S04, S08. Neuroangio cervical outflow examples. Existing IDs: vein.anterior_spinal

fields.Course: Courses within the tentorium between a bridging-vein entry and a transverse, straight or petrosal sinus endpoint.
fields.Tributaries: Cerebellar surface veins; some basal/cerebral venous variants.
fields.Outflow: Transverse, straight or petrosal dural drainage.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Tentorial leaf above cerebellum and below supratentorial brain.
fields.Bone and dura: Free tentorial dura defines most of the channel. Bony attachment applies at petrous/transverse margins, not throughout the leaf.
fields.Required landmarks: Tentorial plane; bridging entry; tentorial attachment; receiving sinus Modelling interpretation Add a flattened intradural route constrained by a tentorial surface. Do not snap it to the occipital or petrous bone along its whole length.
fields.Variants: Highly variable position and tributaries.
fields.Naming: Sinus family, not an extra cerebellar pial vein or a universal persistence of one embryonic channel.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I11, I22. Context and orientation; see source labels
fields.Sources: S01, S04, S11. Bradac pp. 132, 138 and 148; Neuroangio tentorial images.

fields.Course: Links superior/middle peduncular territory with petrosal drainage and lateral mesencephalic connections.
fields.Tributaries: Peduncular and connected lateral mesencephalic tributaries.
fields.Parenchymal relations: Peduncular surface and trigeminal region.
fields.Bone and dura: Intracisternal near the petrous face; reaches dura only through the petrosal terminal connection.
fields.Required landmarks: Peduncular surface; CN V region; lateral mesencephalic vein; petrosal vein Modelling interpretation Our existing lateral mesencephalic-to-petrosal course may already cover its lower component. Audit and label that segment before adding geometry.
fields.Variants: Can be developed separately from the upper lateral mesencephalic segment.
fields.Naming: Do not use pontotrigeminal as a synonym for the whole lateral mesencephalic vein.
fields.Evidence: Course described; metric geometry still needed
fields.Images: I17. Direct angiographic comparison of upper H and lower G components
fields.Sources: S01, S07. Bradac p. 145; Neuroangio upper/lower lateral mesencephalic components. Existing IDs: vein.lateral_mesencephalic.left, vein.lateral_mesencephalic.right

scope: Page 3 P01-P31; selected representative courses, extensions and skin partitions. Metric geometry is illustrative, not measured from the catalogue. Fine sulcal, nuclear, choroidal and nerve corridor anatomy needs specialist review.
landmarkLimitations: Dentate region inferred within cerebellar white matter; no dedicated dentate nucleus mesh
Inferior medullary velum and choroid plexus of fourth ventricle not independently segmented
Middle and inferior cerebellar peduncles constrained by adjacent registered neural surfaces rather than dedicated meshes
Olive, pyramids, obex and cervical root corridors inferred from gross registered surfaces
tentorialPlacement: Flattened body constrained to registered tentorial leaf, with a small inward centreline offset and retained sinus endpoint.
